lenses.lens: Account side of the running live site in pre-launch mode: who may sign in, the admin's first sign-in and second factor,

findings.title: A new or lost phone: after the fresh code the /mfa page leaves for the workspace and never shows the new authenticator's set-up, so CONTRACT 4's way to replace an authenticator does not work
Phone and recovery codes both lost: no way back for the live admin; the operator unlock keeps the enrolment, and nothing removes one
With the recovery codes locked, the MFA page hides the authenticator-code path and disables Continue, although the authenticator still works
Resend's bounce and complaint webhook is not wired: no RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET on edge-bff-live, so every delivery answers 401 and email_suppression is never filled
Pre-launch: a non-test account's right password counts as a failed sign-in; the 11th try shows the rate limit instead of SIGN_IN_CLOSED, and the count outlives the launch
The live web process holds the admin's plaintext first password and address (EDGE_ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD, EDGE_ADMIN_EMAIL) although it never reads them

lenses.lens: A visitor without an account on https://app.edgefinance.id: the pages in a real browser (1440 px and 390 px), every page

findings.title: A visitor's Terminal shows the locked datasets as if there were no data: Flow 'Rp 0', 'No broker data for this ticker', 0 events, 'No 1H data is published for BBCA', and no note that the history is cut to 730 days
The live site now deploys from branch `main` with Wait-for-CI off, not from `live` with checks on: the next push to main goes to app.edgefinance.id ungated
The live site, the only site that sends email, has no RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET: every bounce and complaint webhook is refused and the suppression list never fills
The Privacy and Terms links on every public page lead nowhere
The Terminal shows developer notes to every visitor: 'Market Lab · TradingView-like layout' and 'Standalone Lightweight Charts · Wheel zoom · Drag pan · Y-axis drag scale'
Every visitor behind one public address (a carrier NAT) shares one guest quota of 60 files per hour; a fresh Terminal open spends 5 of them

lenses.lens: State the beta and the live site share, and whether either site can disturb the other: edge_bff.jobs and backtest_jobs b

findings.title: Whichever site holds the shared backtest-worker slot takes it again before the other site can: a queue of jobs on one site holds back the other site's jobs, shown as RUNNING the whole time
Two live variables still read backtest-worker through edge-bff, and the consumer script misses that second step, so a worker change redeployed by the AGENTS.md procedure reaches the beta only
The live site sets no total limit on visitors' Terminal calls, and terminal-api is shared with the beta and the workers

lenses.lens: How the live site is run and rolled back: Railway settings against .railway/railway.ts, the deploy path before and after

findings.title: GitHub main and live do not hold the switch-on: main's railway.ts would delete edge-bff-live, and the running restart cron's code exists only on the session branch
Nobody is told when the live site is down, a live deploy is skipped or fails, or its email or housekeeping fails
Railway labels every edge-bff log line 'error', so a real failure cannot be told from a start-up line
The S7 fix makes the restart's final report depend on a Railway API call after Postgres is back; if it fails, Telegram says Postgres did not come back, or stops at 'started'
EXEC option A's rollback, as written today: no service named, not durable against a push to live, a domain removal the agent cannot undo, step 3's job not prepared, and no way back written
Only procedure guards what reaches the public site: branch `live` is unprotected, and a CLI upload to edge-bff-live skips both `live` and CI
Two live references are still chains, so a change at backtest-worker reaches the beta but not the live site
The live site sends through Resend without its bounce and complaint webhook, so suppression never fills
Some records lag the running site
The admin's first password sits in the live site's process environment, on the internet-facing service
The twice-daily Postgres restart and the live site's cost guards were set for an admin-only beta, not a public site
